general.temas: The death of Gianni De Gennaro, the investigation into alleged efforts to misdirect the inquiry into the Via D’Amelio massacre, and the reactions of public officials dominate four front pages. Measures affecting students and protests, the murder of a pub owner in Turin, and some sports news also appear repeatedly. Only Corriere della Sera highlights the case of Ligurian governor Giovanni Toti and his ties to businessman Spinelli.
general.motivo_crispacion: De Gennaro’s death is a major source of tension because of accusations directed at prosecutors and the debate over the investigation into his alleged role in misdirecting the inquiry. Brothers of Italy’s proposals concerning students under investigation and demonstrations pit the party against the opposition. Corriere della Sera also reports on clashes within the governing majority and controversies in Liguria. Sports, tributes and cultural stories provide some less contentious news.

Corriere della Sera.resumen:
- A headline says the reform of the highway code would not reduce the number of victims.
- The front page highlights conversations and meetings on a yacht between Toti and businessman Spinelli, as well as the defense offered by Genoa Mayor Marco Bucci.
- According to prosecutors, pandemic data was manipulated in Liguria.
- The front page reports tensions within the governing majority over the Superbonus and the tax on drinks, as well as criticism of borrowing.
- It also covers the Russian advance toward Kharkiv, news about Fedez and Camila Giorgi, and investment advice.
Corriere della Sera.motivo_populismo: The coverage is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “the case erupts,” “attack” and “pursued by the tax authorities” add drama and emphasize conflict.
Corriere della Sera.sesgo: The front page gives particular prominence to alleged irregularities involving Ligurian leaders and disagreements within the governing majority. Some headlines take a critical approach, including those concerning road reform and borrowing.

la Repubblica.resumen:
- The death of former police chief Gianni De Gennaro dominates the front page: the circumstances are being investigated and reactions are reported.
- Amendments from FdI that would tighten measures against students and protesters are highlighted.
- Lazio beats Lecce 3-0 and remains top of the table; the front page also covers a possible knee operation for Sinner.
- The front page reports the deaths of jeweler Paolo Bulgari and designer Raffaella Curiel, and the farewell to Augias.
- A study suggests that Leonardo left some works unfinished to preserve his freedom from his patrons.
la Repubblica.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “crackdown” and “must save his knee,” and the emphasis on details of the suicide, add drama and simplification.
la Repubblica.sesgo: The selection and wording focus on the restrictive consequences of FdI’s proposals for students and protesters. Various reactions to De Gennaro are reported, although the coverage devotes extensive space to the circumstances of his death.

La Stampa.resumen:
- Prosecutors in Grosseto are investigating possible incitement to suicide following the death of former police chief Gianni De Gennaro.
- The front page reports reactions from political leaders, Borsellino’s relatives and De Gennaro’s lawyer, alongside accounts of his final days.
- Several pieces examine his relationship with the investigations into the Via D’Amelio massacre and his career alongside figures such as Falcone and Buscetta.
- An employee has been arrested after the owner of a Turin pub was beaten to death; those close to the owner remember him.
- Alcaraz reaches the ATP Finals final, and the drug trafficker known as El Chapo Isidro is captured in Mexico.
La Stampa.motivo_populismo: The coverage is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “the secrets” and “the poisons” or “the broken heart” add drama and sensationalism, without a sustained confrontation between the people and the elites.
La Stampa.sesgo: The front page focuses on De Gennaro’s death and gives space to accounts that show affection for him and to criticism of institutions. It also highlights unanswered questions about the Via D’Amelio massacre, so no clear political slant is apparent.

Il Giornale.resumen:
- Former police chief Gianni De Gennaro died by suicide; he was under investigation over the misdirection of the inquiry into the massacre that killed Borsellino.
- The front page reports political reactions and accusations concerning the circumstances of his death, as well as reviewing the investigation.
- One headline presents a “new truth” about Berlusconi and refers to a period of slander and defamation.
- Tension is growing in Europe over Russian missiles in Poland and a plot in Denmark; a drone alert at Sigonella is also under investigation.
- Schettino is released from prison under social services supervision; other headlines cover protests and participation in a strike.
Il Giornale.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines appear alongside emotional and confrontational expressions such as “the darkest day,” “does not stop even in the face of death” and “demolishes Landini.”
Il Giornale.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach favorable to De Gennaro and Berlusconi, with prominent space given to their defenses. A critical tone toward Communist Refoundation and Landini is also apparent.

Il Fatto Quotidiano.resumen:
- Gianni De Gennaro’s death is the focus of several stories: La Russa’s statements, the investigation and the former police chief’s career.
- FdI proposes suspending aid to students under investigation for crimes related to protests; Conte criticizes the measure.
- Thousands bid farewell to Corrado Augias in Rome; in Turin, an employee has been arrested over the death of a pub owner.
- A court suspends restrictions on assistance to migrants in Trieste. A Concordia survivor speaks about Schettino.
- In sports, Alcaraz talks about his game, and Bolelli and Vavassori split up. A documentary about Kate Middleton is also highlighted.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.motivo_populismo: There are emotive formulations such as “the era of the golden pair comes to an end” and a political contrast in the quote “repression for those who protest and a shield for those in Parliament,” although informative headlines predominate.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.sesgo: The front page pays particular attention to De Gennaro’s death and career and presents FdI’s measures alongside criticism from Conte. It also highlights a ruling favorable to assistance for migrants, though that alone is not enough to attribute a clear political slant to the coverage as a whole.

opiniones.comunista:
I see the proposal to suspend scholarships for students under investigation over acts related to protests as a class-based decision: someone who relies on that aid to study could pay the price even before their responsibility is established. The presumption of innocence and the right to protest should not apply only to those with resources.

I also find it significant that a court in Trieste has suspended restrictions on assistance to migrants. Solidarity is not a public order problem: it is a necessity that institutions must support with adequate public services.

In the face of politics that threatens rights and leaves basic needs to charity, I stand for working-class organization and collective ownership of essential resources. It is not enough to ask big capital to be generous: economic decisions must be placed under the democratic control of those who produce and sustain society.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I am concerned that it is being proposed to suspend scholarships for students who are merely under investigation over acts related to protests. There is no need to wait for a conviction for fear of losing the ability to study to discourage participation. I do not trust parties acting from above to protect a freedom they can restrict when it becomes inconvenient for them. Defending it requires autonomous organization, open assemblies and material support among those who study and work.

In Trieste, the court’s suspension of bans on assistance to migrants reveals another tension: solidarity should not depend on permission from the authorities. I prefer a society in which people can organize help directly, without hierarchies deciding who deserves to receive it. Individual freedom needs collective ties; mutual aid, in turn, loses its meaning if it becomes obedience.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned by the proposal to suspend scholarships for students simply because they are under investigation over acts related to protests. Defending the freedom to demonstrate does not mean tolerating damage: those who cause it must be held accountable. But an investigation is not a conviction, and the state should not turn it into punishment in advance. The presumption of innocence also protects those who make us uncomfortable.

On the economy, the clash over the Superbonus and the tax on drinks is a reminder of why I support stable rules and low taxes. Changing conditions retroactively erodes the confidence needed to invest; adding taxes reduces the freedom of families and businesses to make their own decisions. I prefer a limited state that honors its commitments and controls spending, rather than piling up debt without considering who will have to pay it. Freedom demands responsibility, including in public finances.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I do not want an Italy where state authority is confused with the spectacle of headlines. The death of the former police chief, who was under investigation for an alleged cover-up in the case of the Via D’Amelio massacre, demands respect and a rigorous investigation, not media verdicts. The presumption of innocence protects everyone; the search for truth is also a duty owed to the victims.

I support public order and holding those who cause damage during occupations accountable. But withdrawing scholarships merely because someone is under investigation means punishing them before guilt is proven. And in Trieste, providing humanitarian assistance to migrants should not prevent the state from controlling its borders and deciding who enters and stays. Sovereignty demands firmness, but also institutions that respect their own rules.
opiniones.centro:
Gianni De Gennaro’s death deserves respect and caution, not a hasty political judgment. I believe that defending the presumption of innocence and seeking the truth about the alleged misdirection of the Via D’Amelio investigation are compatible duties. Justice must be allowed to work without pressure, and families have a right to answers based on evidence.

That is also why I am concerned about the proposal to suspend scholarships for students under investigation over acts related to protests. Causing damage must have consequences, but an investigation is not equivalent to a conviction, and withdrawing aid before the facts are established can unfairly punish people and make it harder for them to pursue their studies. I would seek a consensus to ensure safety and repair the damage without turning suspicion into a penalty. Institutions grow stronger when they protect rights even in moments of tension.
